
From the arXiv RSS signals, EEG-PRISM (2608.13676) is a strong new addition applying transformer foundation models to EEG physiological signals with interpretability analysis — clearly non-NLP, domain-grounded, and empirically evaluated. ProtGPT2 from the Grok signals is a legitimate protein design transformer not yet in the README, though it is older (2022). The histopathology ViT signal has a fake arXiv ID and is excluded. Most other arXiv signals are NLP/LLM-focused or general ML methods without domain-specific transformer application.

## Suggestions

- [EEG-PRISM: Physiologically-Grounded Interpretability of EEG Foundation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13676) — Transformer-based EEG foundation model with physiologically-grounded interpretability framework for brain signal classification and analysis.
  Section: Time-Series & Signals | Criteria: Applies transformer architecture to EEG physiological signals (non-NLP domain), Addresses domain-specific task: EEG signal classification and foundation model interpretability, Iterative modeling grounded in EEG domain data, Empirical evaluation of foundation model predictions on physiological benchmarks

- [ProtGPT2: Deep Unsupervised Language Model for Protein Design](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-022-01398-9) — GPT-2-style autoregressive transformer trained on UniRef50 for de novo protein sequence generation, producing sequences with natural-like structural properties.
  Section: Protein & Molecular Structure | Criteria: Applies transformer (GPT-2 decoder) to protein sequences — non-NLP domain, Addresses protein design task with measurable sequence quality and structural plausibility metrics, Trained on UniRef50 protein sequence corpus with iterative autoregressive modeling, Empirical benchmarking against natural protein distributions and AlphaFold structure validation
